The run stalled at Step 5. Here's what happened:

**Implementation complete** — Cursor committed changes on branch `sergey-zhupanov/implementing-stop-shrinking-judge-panel-2643` (sha `aa45a488`), relevant checks passed, but the review wrapper returned `STALL_REASON=round-failed-complete` after round 1 completed with 0 findings.

The review round itself succeeded (0 accepted, 0 rejected findings) but the Step 5 loop wrapper couldn't continue past it. This appears to be an internal wrapper state issue unrelated to the actual implementation quality.

**To recover**: re-run `/larch:im 2643` — the session-entry-gate will detect the existing `sergey-zhupanov/implementing-stop-shrinking-judge-panel-2643` branch and resume from there, skipping re-implementation and re-entering at Step 5.

Issue #2643 has been renamed to `[STALLED]`.
cause of stall?

Found it. Line 155–159 is the catch-all `*` branch — `IRF_LAST_ROUND_STATUS=complete` fell through to it because `complete` is not in the recognized set at line 150–154.

The loop only recognizes these round-end statuses as success: `converged-small-changes`, `no-changes`, `no-findings`, `in-scope-filtered-out`, `fix-applied`. When `review-and-fix.sh` emits `REVIEW_AND_FIX_STATUS=complete` (0 findings), the loop treats it as an unrecognized status and emits `round-failed-complete` → stall.

Let me verify that's the actual value propagated:

Confirmed. The bug chain:

1. `review-and-fix.sh` line 1230: when `core_status=zero-findings|ok` (0 findings), it sets `status="complete"` → emits `REVIEW_AND_FIX_STATUS=complete`.
2. `review-implement-step5-loop.sh` line 150: the recognized success statuses are `converged-small-changes|no-changes|no-findings|in-scope-filtered-out|fix-applied`. **`complete` is absent.**
3. `complete` falls to the `*` catch-all at line 156 → `round-failed-complete` stall.

The fix is one line — add `complete` to the case arm at line 150:

```bash
converged-small-changes|no-changes|no-findings|in-scope-filtered-out|complete)
```

`no-findings` and `complete` both mean "0 findings, nothing to do" but come from different exit paths inside `review-and-fix.sh` — the loop only handled the former. This only surfaces when the implementation is clean enough that the reviewer panel finds nothing at all.
make this fix in this same PR, and recover and keep going -- we need to land this!
